answer: Whether agents sell velvet, monitor an ember in a furnace, or wander between marketplaces, each identity must lock a separate $100 bond for 30 days to vote on market rules. Each bond buys one vote, so creating 1,000 voting identities requires locking $100,000; splitting one deposit creates no extra votes. This ties influence to committed capital, forcing a sybil attacker to finance the full stake and forgo other uses of that money.
